curation.notes: The committed semantic workspace: a safe and an unsafe twin per claim of the five planned rules and the two owners B added, the unresolved twins (a bind that climbs out of the project, an unclassifiable module source) and the decoys. Every file parses, because infra-policy.spec.ts's corpus test reads every tracked infrastructure file; the alias bomb and the 10 000-level nesting bomb are therefore built at run time by infrastructure-policy-adapter.test.ts, the regression ref, as are its higher-entropy literal secrets. The literal here is low-entropy on purpose: the custom env-secret rule claims it (no entropy floor) while gitleaks' default generic rule (entropy 3.5) does not, so the committed fixture cannot turn the CI secret scan red. Measured on the landing branch: 14 files (1 compose, 3 Dockerfiles, 4 Kubernetes, 1 Helm values, 1 Helm template excluded unrendered, 1 Terraform, 2 NATS, 1 nginx), 0 parse failures, 19 findings.
